lines.text: Job longs for the days when God watched over him and the friendship of God rested on his tent.
When Job took his seat in the public square, the young men withdrew and the princes covered their mouths with their hands.
Job rescued the poor who cried out, and he was eyes to the blind and ears to the lame.
Younger men now mock Job, and Job would have refused to put their fathers with his camels.
God throws Job into the mud, and Job says he has become a brother of jackals and a companion of ostriches.
